brief: Privorotsky reads yesterday as several complications converging. Energy broke higher, rates followed, PPI was hot with hospitals and airfares firm enough for GIR to nudge core PCE up 2bps, and CPI prints today with .25 on core as the September dividing line. He argues the Fed is cornered: with 35-50% of a hike priced post-CPI, not hiking would be punitive for the back end, so a modestly higher .26-.28 print that forces full September pricing may be cleaner and could pull hikes forward rather than add to the almost 90bps priced to Dec 27. Treasury bought back $5.2bn against a $6bn cap, which he reads two ways, sensible price discipline or counterproductive visible price sensitivity. The ECB hiked 25bp with a hawkish conference and higher projections, moving European rates multiple sigma. Oracle's OCI +121%, 97.9% GPU utilization and $664bn RPO show compute scarce and pricing rising while token pricing collapses, still supportive for hardware, with DeepSeek V4.1 efficiency the wrinkle. Houthi advances at Mocha and the Hanish Islands make the Gulf and Red Sea exit routes a two front problem. Equities are resilient with oil near $110 and 10s near 5%, and he thinks much is already priced.
